ai.description: This small frog measures 25–30 mm. It is brownish-grey with a distinct, pointed snout and prominent, bulging eyes. Key features include a granular dorsal texture and a lack of webbing on the feet.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Dattatreya Night Frog is best distinguished by its unique, fleshy, elongated snout tip that extends significantly beyond the mouth, unlike other *Nyctibatrachus* species.
ai.habitat: The Dattatreya Night Frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, specifically found near rocky streams at elevations above 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Dattatreya Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden in rock crevices or under leaf litter during the day to avoid predators and desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus dattatreyaensis* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of 20–30 large, unpigmented eggs in rock crevices or near streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Dattatreya Night Frog is endemic to the high-altitude evergreen forests of the Western Ghats in Karnataka, specifically found at elevations above 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Dattatreya Night Frog produces a high-pitched, insect-like "tseep" call, typically heard during the monsoon season near fast-flowing streams in the Western Ghats.
